items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: The name 'GW' appears only as a label for the [INTERVIEWER] in the transcript header and within the interviewer's turn ('GW: Yeah well...'). There is no mention of a personal relationship between the interviewee and GW beyond the standard interviewer-interviewee dynamic.

ctx.x: I think it’s probably the same way. I’m sure that I don’t worry about it. I just don’t worry about it. It’s like if a guy wants to hire me I’m there for the music. I go in, I try to do the best I can for what the situation warrants. Hopefully when people hire me they trust me to bring forth what I can do. And I’m there for the good of the music. And I try to get along with everybody, there we go again, Kum-ba-ya baby, that’s what you want. That’s what it’s all supposed to be. You know music is supposed to be a…

Right. Well said. Let’s suppose you got asked to do a career day at a local high school and would you be encouraging to some aspiring musicians to try to make a living in this day and age? GW: Yeah well that’s an interesting comment because I was walking down the hall of Oberlin where I teach and I was listening to all of these people play this phenomenal, you know like I wish I could play the piano like this, it’s just ridiculous, and you have a violinist over here, and I was thinking what are they all going to…

give them that vibe and who knows what they can do until they get out there and try. I’m going to try to get them better. I’m going to sit there and play with them and work on their reaction time and work on their ears and try to play something back to them that they fall apart trying to play back to me so they’ll get better. So that they’ll go out there and see what they can do. Because that’s really what, you know I think that’s a big problem sometimes with say families where you have the family negative…
